taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and native to Texas at state scale.
look_here_first: BIGTOP LOVEGRASS: large open panicle, perennial tussock, but the much better first character is long HAIRS present over the leaf SHEATH BODY and margins (not only around the mouth). The actual source-image inspection shows those hairs on two sheaths. Lower panicle branch-axil tufts support ID when visible; missing in current macros. Compare with relatively smoother-sheathed plains and throat-hairy sand lovegrass; no cloudlike seedhead alone proves species.

morphology_keys.what_to_teach_crew: Hairy across the sheath = think BIGTOP. Hair only at the opening does not prove bigtop. Use a sheath closeup, the open inflorescence and axils together; compare plains and sand lovegrass rather than guessing by color.
overlap_cautions: Collar hairs alone occur in E. intermedia and E. trichodes; the distribution of hairs over the sheath surface is more informative.
A fuzzy-looking inflorescence is not proof of E. hirsuta; panicle branch axils must actually be inspected.
Native statewide does not establish nativity in Hays County; current target-zone native-range verdict remains unresolved.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with E. intermedia and E. trichodes, examine several complete leaf sheaths: E. hirsuta has conspicuous hairs ON THE SHEATH SURFACE, not only concentrated at the sheath throat. Pair this with lower panicle axil beard and broad open panicle; E. spectabilis has a striking wide, often purple inflorescence but is not identified by color.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Bigtop lovegrass: sheath first, panicle second
steps: START WITH THE SHEATH: use stored Becky Dill photo to locate hairs on sheath body and sheath mouth. For E. hirsuta, Kew describes hirsute sheaths with hairy outer margins and oral hairs. Do not label every visible hair 'ligule'.

AT THE TRUE COLLAR: unfold a mature blade and separately photograph the short LIGULE FRINGE OF HAIRS at 10–20× beside a 1-mm scale, distinguishing it from longer surrounding sheath-mouth hairs. Existing photo 0 does not expose a measured ligule.

CHECK OPEN BIGTOP PANICLE using archived Cleveland Powell views 1 and 2: Kew reports broadly ovate open heads around 25–60 cm long and 15–25 cm wide; capture whole outline and lower primary branch junctions, rather than merely photographing a purple haze.

PANICLE BRANCH AXILS: Kew reports the primary branches bearded in the axils. This remains UNPROVEN by archived views; isolate the actual branch insertion with magnification and don't aim an arrow at unrelated hairs.

MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS: Kew describes solitary pedicelled, laterally compressed spikelets about 2–4 mm long and 1–1.2 mm wide, with 2–6 fertile florets. Photograph attached head plus isolated spikelet with 1-mm rule.

CHECK LOOK-ALIKES: E. intermedia, E. trichodes and E. spectabilis require matching sheath hair distribution, branch axil hairs and counted spikelets, not just a wide panicle. Keep ID provisional when decisive organs are invisible.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Sheath BODY and MARGIN hair + hair-fringe true ligule + BEARDED primary branch axils + open large panicle; verify tiny 2–4 mm multi-flowered spikelets on a single mature specimen.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: New Douglas Goldman exact-species CC BY-SA photographs visually screened for sheath hairs, true bearded panicle branch axil, and attached single spikelet; do not infer short inner ligule margin or calibrated florets. All markers withheld pending full-resolution precise pixel placement.
